panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel-specific caption states this is an example of a plague bubo that is enlarged. Ultrasound image shows enlarged hypoechoic node, consistent with plague_bubo vocabulary. B: Disease-focused article on morphology of buboes in bubonic plague plus panel-specific abnormal lymph-node description supports attribution to plague bubo with radiological progression; image shows round abnormal node with loss of hilum.
panels.attribution_text: Bourner et al. A prospective cohort study to describe the morphology of buboes in patients with bubonic plague using ultrasound imaging.. PLoS neglected tropical diseases 2026. doi:10.1371/journal.pntd.0014133. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Normal and abnormal lymph node features. A) An example of a plague bubo without abnormal radiological findings. While enlarged, this lymph node exhibits relatively normal features including a well-defined, oval-shaped capsule with a distinct echogenic hilum and normal surrounding perinodal tissue. B) Anomalous findings on ultrasound indicative radiological progression would include blurring to the edges of the capsule (which may be indicative of oedema), a circular-shaped capsule, a decrease in the size of the hilum or a total absence of the hilum.
in_text_mentions: Butterfly iQ+ probe (iQ, Butterfly Network, Inc, Guilford, CT, USA) and included evaluation of nodal shape (oval or round), capsule (distinct or blurred), hilum appearance (visible or obscured), cortex (homogenous or irregular), presence of necrosis, hypervascularity, perinodal reactivity, and coalescence. A summary of the sonographic features evaluated in the study can be seen in Fig 1. Still images and cine clips of the index node were captured on D1, D4 and D11 for subsequent QA review by two experienced radiologists. Node measurements were obtained using the Butterfly iQ+ measurement tool.

The majority of plague buboes exhibited normal structural characteristics (Fig 1) on ultrasound. More than half of the buboes were oval-shaped (67%), had a distinct capsule (56%) and homogeneous cortex (56%), and just under half had a distinct hilum (44%). Few buboes exhibited severe structural anomalies such as necrosis (11%), hypervascularity (22%) and coalescence (11%) (Fig 3).
